notFound.title: Page not found

content.noticeLong: The interface is now in English, but the curriculum itself — lessons, flashcards and questions — is still written in Vietnamese.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.intro: Eleven tracks, ordered by dependency. You can go out of order, but every track assumes the ones before it — skipping ahead usually costs more time than it saves.

review.emptyFresh: Flashcards appear once you finish your first lesson. The system brings them back exactly when you are about to forget them.
review.emptyHealthy: Your memory is in good shape. Reviewing more right now costs time without adding anything — that is the model's conclusion, not a consolation.
review.doneSub: {n} reviews in {time}. What you just did will hold this knowledge for several more weeks.
review.adviceTooEasy: You recalled almost everything. That sounds good, but it means the system is showing you cards too early — you are spending time on things you did not need yet. Try lowering target retention to 0.85 in Settings.
review.adviceTooHard: Your forgetting rate is a little high. You may be taking on new material faster than you can consolidate it. Try lowering new cards per day, or re-read the parts you keep forgetting.
review.adviceOptimal: Your recall rate is in the optimal band (roughly 85–92%). Forgetting a little is a good sign: it means each review is actually doing something for your memory.
review.tryRecall: Try to recall first — the struggle itself is what strengthens the memory.
review.gradeHonestly: Grade honestly. Pressing "Easy" for a card you actually thought about for 5 seconds only sabotages your own schedule.

practice.emptySub: Practice draws questions from lessons you have opened. Study your first lesson first.
practice.title: Practice
practice.intro: Applied questions, mixed across topics. Harder than flashcards — which is exactly why it builds real skill better.
practice.modeAutoDesc: 60% from your weak spots, 40% random so the rest does not fade.
practice.modeAllDesc: Fully random across every lesson you have studied. Closest to the real thing.
practice.masterySub: Scores decay over time if you do not revisit a concept — this is the app telling you the truth instead of handing out a permanent green tick.
practice.resultNote: Interleaved scores usually come out lower than practising one lesson at a time. That is normal, and it is a good sign: you just trained the hardest skill of all — recognising what kind of problem you are looking at with no hint up front.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: Every term carries both its Vietnamese and English name — industry documentation and every tool use English, so knowing both is mandatory.
glossary.emptySub: Try a shorter keyword, or clear the tag filter.

labs.title: Labs
labs.intro: Real models running in JavaScript inside your browser. No server, no data leaving your machine. Turn the knobs and watch how the system breaks.
labs.buildingSub: This exercise is still being built.

grade.2desc: Recalled, but it was a struggle

plan.goalMet: You hit today's {goal}-minute goal. Anything more is a bonus, not a duty.
plan.fresh: Nothing due. {n} new cards are waiting to enter long-term memory.
plan.nextLesson: Your memory is healthy. Good moment for a new lesson: {title}.

calibration.overconfident: You are OVERCONFIDENT: your real accuracy is well below what you think it is. This is the most dangerous kind of gap, because you will never choose to review it.
calibration.underconfident: You are UNDERCONFIDENT: you know more than you think. Be bolder, and stop re-reviewing what you already have.
calibration.wellCalibrated: Your self-assessment is well calibrated — the mark of a mature learner.

badge.streak-30Desc: Study 30 days in a row — the habit has formed
badge.lab-ratDesc: Open and play with 10 different labs

home.reviewFirstSub: These cards are right at the edge of forgetting. Skipping today lets the earlier effort evaporate.
home.overflow: {n} cards exceed today's cap and roll over to tomorrow. That cap exists so you never get buried.
home.firstLessonSub: No prior knowledge needed. The first lesson takes 14 minutes.
home.drillSub: {n} questions mixed across tracks, weighted toward your weak spots.
home.goalMet: Met — the rest is a bonus
home.streakBroken: Your longest streak: {n} days. A day off does not erase what you learned — the review system is still there.
home.introHead: This app works differently from courses you have seen
home.p1d: You will be asked things you cannot answer yet. Guessing wrong and then reading the explanation sticks better than reading it straight — that is a research finding, not a style choice.
home.p2d: The system estimates the day each idea is about to slip and brings it back exactly then. You never have to remember what to review.
home.p3d: 24 labs run real models in your browser. Dragging one slider and watching a detector collapse teaches faster than ten pages of prose.
home.p4d: Every lesson states where the knowledge is used in real work, who uses it, and what breaks if you do not know it.
home.p5d: The app tracks whether you know what you know. Overconfidence is the most dangerous gap, because you never go back to it.
home.p6d: The stated duration of each lesson is honest. Nothing is padded to fill space.

progress.title: Progress
progress.intro: This page deliberately shows your weak spots, not just your wins. An all-green dashboard makes people stop reviewing — and discover three months later that it is all gone.
progress.avgRetentionOn: Average recall probability across {n} tracked cards.
progress.forecastSub: See it coming so a mountain of cards never surprises you
progress.heaviestDay: Heaviest day: {n} cards. If this climbs too high, lower the new-cards-per-day quota in Settings — that is the only way to keep the schedule sustainable.
progress.calibTitle: Do you know what you know?
progress.calibSub: Your stated confidence against your actual accuracy
progress.weakSub: Scores decay over time if you do not revisit them — that is the truth, not a punishment
progress.badgesSub: Every one is tied to a good study habit — none rewards a 5-hour cramming session

settings.title: Settings
settings.themeHint: Dark mode uses #0f1117 rather than pure black — maximum contrast makes white text bloom, which is especially harsh for readers with astigmatism.
settings.fontSizeHint: If you are squinting or leaning toward the screen, turn this up. Eye strain measurably reduces how much you take in.
settings.reduceMotionHint: For anyone sensitive to motion (vestibular disorders, migraine) — or who simply prefers things still.
settings.dailyGoalHint: Pick a number you can hold on your busiest day. An ambitious goal missed a few times turns into quitting entirely.
settings.newCardsHint: This is the most important knob on the page. 60 new cards today means 60 cards due in a few days, stacked on top of the old ones. Do that a few times and you have a review debt mountain — the number one reason people abandon spaced-repetition apps.
settings.maxReviewsHint: A safety ceiling for busy days. Anything over the cap rolls to tomorrow automatically.
settings.targetRetentionHint: 0.90 is the best balance between time spent and knowledge held. Pushing to 0.95 makes review counts spike for a marginal gain — worth it only when you are preparing for a specific exam.
settings.showIntervals: Show next interval on grading buttons
settings.askConfidenceHint: This trains self-assessment — the skill that decides whether you review the right things. Turning it off speeds up sessions but costs you the calibration chart on the Progress page.
settings.dataIntro: All progress lives in this browser, with no copy anywhere else. Clearing browsing data, using private mode, or switching machines wipes it.
settings.confirmLearning: This erases all lesson progress, flashcards and statistics, but keeps your preferences.
settings.confirmAll: This erases EVERYTHING: progress, cards, notes, preferences. The app returns to a fresh install.
settings.auditOk: Every lesson meets the required criteria
settings.importWrongFormat: That file is not an AEGIS progress file.
settings.importBadJson: Could not read the JSON file.
settings.importEmpty: The file is valid but contains no progress. You may have picked the wrong file.
settings.importConfirmTitle: Importing will replace all of your current progress
settings.importUndone: Restored the progress you had before importing.

onboarding.title: Machine Learning for Security
onboarding.intro: From knowing nothing to building and evaluating a detection system yourself. No prior maths or programming required.
onboarding.goalHead: How much time do you have each day?
onboarding.goalSub: Pick the number you can certainly hold, not the one you wish for. The app builds a plan that fits it. A steady 20 minutes beats 3 hours crammed into Sunday, every time — and that is an evidence-backed finding, not a platitude.
onboarding.knowHead: A few things to know first
onboarding.recallTitle: This app makes you recall, not just read
onboarding.recallBody: You will meet questions before the explanation, and cards will return exactly when you are about to forget. It feels harder than skimming — that is the point, and it is why you will still remember six months later.
onboarding.privacyTitle: Your data stays on your machine
onboarding.privacyBody: No account, no server, no tracking. All progress lives in this browser. Head to Settings to export a backup before you switch machines or clear browsing data.
onboarding.nameLabel: Your name (optional, stored only on your machine)
onboarding.goal10d: Just enough to keep momentum. Fine for very busy people.
onboarding.goal20d: The best balance for most people.
onboarding.goal35d: Fast progress; needs a fairly regular slot.
onboarding.goal60d: A serious career move, with time clearly set aside.
onboarding.o1: Explain why "99.9% accuracy" is usually a meaningless number in security
onboarding.o2: Choose the algorithm, features and threshold for a specific detection problem
onboarding.o3: Recognise and defend against attacks aimed directly at your model
onboarding.o4: Protect LLM applications from prompt injection and agent risks

lesson.whyCost: If you do not know it
lesson.quizSub: {n} questions. This is not about grading you — the act of retrieving is what turns what you just read into knowledge you keep. Re-reading feels nicer and does almost nothing.
lesson.notesHint: Putting it in your own words is one of the strongest memory techniques — stronger than highlighting or copying verbatim. Try answering: "If I had 30 seconds to explain this to a colleague, what would I say?"
lesson.notesPlaceholder: Write it in your own words…
lesson.cardsSub: These will come back exactly when you are about to forget
lesson.prereqBody: You can still read on — it will just be harder than it needs to be.
lesson.whyCostHead: What happens if you do not know it
lesson.objectivesHead: By the end of this lesson you will
lesson.notesAutoSave: Saved automatically when you click away.
lesson.furtherHead: Further reading, if you want to dig in
lesson.cardsFromLessonSub: Once you take the check, the system brings them back exactly when you are about to forget.

quiz.confidencePrompt: Before you answer: how sure are you?
quiz.multiHint: More than one answer may be correct.
quiz.orderPrompt: Click them in the right order
quiz.sureButWrong: You were certain and wrong — the most dangerous kind of gap, because you will never choose to review it. Read the explanation below carefully.
quiz.knewMore: You know more than you thought — next time, trust your reasoning a little more.
quiz.resultGood: You have this lesson down. The flashcards will move it into long-term memory over the next few weeks.
quiz.resultMid: The foundation is there but there are gaps. Do not redo the whole lesson — let the review system bring back exactly what you missed.
quiz.resultLow: This one needs another read. That is fine: finding out now is far cheaper than finding out in an interview or during a real incident.

blocks.reveal: I have thought about it — show me
blocks.predictHint: Think for real, even ten seconds. Guessing wrong and then reading the explanation sticks longer than reading the answer straight.
blocks.checkpointHint: Answer before reading on — this is where the knowledge gets anchored.

backup.nudgeStale: Your last backup was {when}. You have learned a fair bit since then.
backup.writeFailed: Could not save your progress to this browser — most likely out of storage space. Export a backup now so you do not lose this session.
backup.recoverTitle: Could not read your learning data
backup.recoverBody: The original ({kb} KB) was preserved instead of being overwritten. Download it — if only a few characters are damaged it can still be repaired by hand.
backup.recoverDiscard: I have it, discard this copy
